## Excursions to Agoyán Waterfall from Baños

[Agoyán Waterfall](/ecuador/place/agoyan-waterfall/) lies in the Pastaza River valley near the Ecuadorian town of Baños. Here water runs between rocky walls covered in humid vegetation. As you travel east of the town, the scenery changes from the high Andes to a warmer, greener valley.

Agoyán is part of the **Waterfall Route**, linking several natural attractions. Ada Tours offers two excursions that visit this site. The most useful first decision is where your journey will continue after Baños.

## Two itinerary options

| Excursion | Duration and ending point |
|---|---|
| [Baños, waterfalls and the swing](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-swing/) | 8–9 hours, ending with a transfer to Riobamba |
| [Waterfalls with return to Quito](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-return-to-quito/) | 11–12 hours including transfers, ending in Quito |

Both programs include an introduction to Baños followed by **Agoyán**, Bride's Veil and Devil's Cauldron waterfalls, the Pastaza Canyon and the Swing at the End of the World. These are distinct natural attractions, not alternative names for one cascade.

## Excursion ending in Riobamba

[Baños: the Waterfall Route and the Swing at the End of the World](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-swing/) lasts **8–9 hours**, including travel. After breakfast, guests explore Baños and then follow the Pastaza Valley.

The itinerary includes a stop at Agoyán, Bride's Veil with its cable crossing, Devil's Cauldron and the swing at Casa del Árbol. A transfer to Riobamba lasting approximately **2 hours** is planned for the afternoon, followed by hotel check-in.

This option works well if the next stage of your journey takes you through central Ecuador.

## Excursion returning to Quito

[Baños: waterfalls and swing with return to Quito](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-return-to-quito/) visits the same major attractions but ends in the capital. The journey takes **11–12 hours**, including approximately **3.5 hours** for the Baños–Quito drive.

This option therefore involves more time in transportation. Consider the evening return time and how many stops you want to make along the way.

## What to see at Agoyán

The waterfall lies in a mountain gorge. Viewpoints offer scenes of falling water and the surrounding slopes. Further along the Waterfall Route, you can see Bride's Veil, linked in the itinerary to a cable-car crossing, and then Devil's Cauldron.

Both excursions offer an additional option of **canopy activities above the Pastaza Canyon for USD 15 per person**. This is an optional, separately paid activity and should not be assumed to be included.

## Choosing the right day

If Riobamba is your next destination after Baños, select the matching itinerary. If you need to return to Quito, choose the capital-bound option. Both programs have many stops, and time at each waterfall varies with road conditions, weather and the day's schedule.

For more nature-focused journeys, browse [Ecuador tours](/ecuador/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about Agoyán Waterfall

### Is Agoyán included in both Waterfall Route excursions?

Yes. Agoyán features in both the [route to Riobamba](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-swing/) and the [route returning to Quito](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-return-to-quito/).

### How do the excursions differ?

The main differences are **the final city and total day duration**: 8–9 hours with Riobamba versus 11–12 hours with Quito.

### Is canopy included in the price?

No. Both programs offer it as an optional extra at **USD 15 per person**.

### Which excursion includes the Swing at the End of the World?

The swing is included in both options along with the waterfall visits.

## AmaZOOnico excursion: getting to know rescued wildlife

[AmaZOOnico](/ecuador/place/amazoonico-animal-rescue-center/) is in the Ecuadorian Amazon beside the [Arajuno River](/ecuador/place/arajuno-river/). The center receives wild animals harmed by illegal captivity and trade. Animals capable of returning to their natural habitat are prepared for release, while those unable to return remain in the center's care.

For travelers, this is an opportunity to learn how wildlife rescue, rehabilitation and conservation education work. **A visit is not the same as going to a hands-on zoo**: visitors must not feed, stroke or attract animals for photographs.

## Which Ada Tours excursion visits AmaZOOnico?

One of our programs is the [Cosano Forest and AmaZOOnico Animal Rescue Center excursion](/ecuador/cosano-reserve/ecuador-cosano-amazoonico/). It combines an introduction to [Cosano](/ecuador/place/cosano-reserve/) forest, river travel and a visit to the center on the Arajuno.

The boat ride from the lodge to an area of private forest takes around 20 minutes. Walks through the forest last approximately 1 to 3 hours. After hiking, tubing on the river may be possible; a separate stop involves AmaZOOnico. This does not confirm that tubing is always included in every rate. A return to Casa del Suizo by boat is also planned.

The fixed price, guide language and services paid for should be agreed for the particular trip before departure. Do not simply add the forest walking time and the center visit to claim a precise total duration for the whole day.

## What visitors see at the center and why an escort matters

Staff and volunteers tell the stories of animals and explain why some cannot return to the forest. AmaZOOnico may care for monkeys, birds, reptiles and other local wildlife. The mix of animals changes, however, and a visit does not guarantee sightings of particular species.

The purpose is to understand the consequences of illegal wildlife trade and efforts to restore natural populations. The center tries to protect potential release candidates from excessive contact with people, so visitors are not given access to every animal.

The center's official website says visits are accompanied and require advance booking. Current rules and availability on a specific date should be checked when planning the journey.

## How Cosano Forest differs from a visit to AmaZOOnico

| Place | Main focus |
|---|---|
| [Cosano](/ecuador/place/cosano-reserve/) | Forest walk |
| [Arajuno](/ecuador/place/arajuno-river/) | River sections |
| [AmaZOOnico](/ecuador/place/amazoonico-animal-rescue-center/) | Animal rescue |

In the forest, visitors learn about local plants and might see animals living freely. At the center, they learn why some animals are under human care. Do not combine these experiences into promises of the same wildlife sightings.

Viewpoints in Cosano offer river scenery and views toward settlements near Ahuano. If time is limited, decide which activity matters most: a guided walk, the river or the animal rescue center's work.

## Practical advice: clothing and rules

The humid rainforest calls for comfortable shoes you do not mind getting muddy, a raincoat, drinking water and insect protection. Travel on the river depends on the weather and water level. At the center, stay with the group, follow designated trails and take photographs without flash.

Even if an animal comes close, touching it is forbidden. Do not offer food or try to make it look toward your camera. These restrictions protect animal welfare and visitor safety.

Travelers mainly interested in Amazon wildlife can also compare [nature and wildlife journeys](/interests/wildlife/). Actual wildlife encounters and center visits depend on the chosen itinerary, not the broad name of the theme.

## Frequently asked questions about AmaZOOnico

### Is it a petting zoo?

No. The center rescues and rehabilitates wild animals. Visitors may not touch, feed or disturb them.

### Can visitors see animals being prepared for release?

The center limits human contact with animals that may eventually be released, so excursions do not provide access to every animal.

### Is advance booking required?

Yes. AmaZOOnico's official site requires reservations. For an Ada Tours trip, the visiting time is coordinated with the river and forest portions.

### Are the boat ride and forest walk part of the same program?

Our itinerary includes a boat journey and a walk through Cosano Forest. The exact included services, whether tubing is possible and the format of the center visit should be confirmed for the selected trip.

## Arajuno River excursions: boats and forest in the Ecuadorian Amazon

The [Arajuno River](/ecuador/place/arajuno-river/) flows through forested areas of the Ecuadorian Amazon. For travelers, it provides a water route to forest sites, settlements and a wildlife rescue center. An excursion here involves traveling by boat and walking through the forest, rather than merely viewing the river from the bank.

One of our routes is the [Cosano Forest and AmaZOOnico Animal Rescue Center excursion](/ecuador/cosano-reserve/ecuador-cosano-amazoonico/), where the Arajuno is important for both transportation and the natural experience. The geographic name may occur in several accounts of the region, but the excursion offered here is a specific product.

## What the described route includes

The itinerary begins with a boat transfer of approximately 20 minutes to a private forest area, where walks of about 1 to 3 hours are available. Along the trail, the guide shows plants and explains their uses. Viewpoints overlook the surroundings of Ahuano, the Napo River and its tributaries.

After the forest walk, continuing down the Arajuno on inflatable tubes may be possible. The program mentions this as an option, but we do not promise that tubing is included in every version. Agree on the precise activities when planning the day.

The [AmaZOOnico animal rescue center](/ecuador/place/amazoonico-animal-rescue-center/) is located on the Arajuno. A visit offers an introduction to wildlife rescue and rehabilitation. The return boat trip to Casa del Suizo takes approximately 15 minutes.

## River, forest and rescue center: different activities

| Section | Main interest |
|---|---|
| Boat on the Arajuno | River scenery |
| [Cosano Forest](/ecuador/place/cosano-reserve/) | Plants and trails |
| [AmaZOOnico](/ecuador/place/amazoonico-animal-rescue-center/) | Helping animals |

A boat crossing alone does not mean travelers can use every nature trail. Likewise, a rescue center visit does not guarantee wildlife encounters in the free-ranging forest. Decide in advance where you want to spend most of your time.

Visibility of animals in the forest depends on their behavior, while vegetation and humidity make long-distance photography difficult. Even a short walking route can be slippery after heavy rain.

## River tubing on the Arajuno: what to check

Floating on inflatable tubes has different requirements from a regular motorboat ride. Confirm whether tubing is permitted under current conditions, which stretch is used, whether swimming skills are required, whether life jackets are supplied and how the accompanying guide decides based on the water level.

As tubing is only offered as a possible extension, **it must not be assumed to be a guaranteed component** of every Arajuno trip. The activity, safety arrangements and time allocation are agreed separately.

For the boat and walking sections, bring a waterproof document pouch, spare clothing, shoes with good grip and rain protection. Clothes can remain damp into the evening, which is worth considering when packing.

## Where these places are located

The Ahuano area and the Arajuno River lie in Napo Province in the Ecuadorian Amazon. The AmaZOOnico center is on the riverbank, while Cosano Forest is a separate area for exploring local vegetation. The excursion combines them into one route but has its own program and conditions.

If you are interested in nature journeys elsewhere in Ecuador, begin with [nature and wildlife](/interests/wildlife/) and compare actual trips by duration and physical demands. Amazon forests and Galápagos island routes require very different preparation.

## Frequently asked questions about Arajuno excursions

### Can I see animals during the boat ride?

Wildlife encounters are possible, but sightings are not guaranteed. A visit to AmaZOOnico offers a different conservation-focused experience.

### Is tubing always included?

There is no confirmation that it is included in every option. We suggest considering it as a possible continuation of the forest walk.

### How long is the entire excursion?

The source specifies 1–3 hours for forest walks and separate boat transfers, but does not provide a single precise duration for the full day. This should be agreed.

### Should I prepare for rain?

Yes. This is a humid tropical region; non-slip shoes, waterproof protection for belongings and a flexible plan for changing river conditions are important.

## Bachas Beaches excursion: nature on northern Santa Cruz

[Bachas Beaches](/ecuador/place/bachas-beaches/) lie on the north shore of Santa Cruz Island in the Galápagos archipelago. Light sand meets dark volcanic rocks and clear seawater. Small lagoons behind the shore attract waterbirds.

This is a natural stop on a day of marine excursions, not an ordinary resort beach with restaurants and services. Wildlife sightings and sea conditions depend on the natural environment.

## Which Ada Tours excursion includes Bachas?

Our catalog includes a [North Seymour Island and Bachas Beaches excursion](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/north-seymour-island-tour/). It includes a bus transfer to a yacht at the Itabaca Channel, a boat trip to North Seymour and a continuation to Bachas.

[North Seymour Island](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) is known for frigatebirds, blue-footed boobies, dry volcanic scenery and palo santo trees. [Bachas](/ecuador/place/bachas-beaches/) adds a white sandy shore and lagoons. Together, these stops reveal different facets of Galápagos nature in a single trip.

Our excursion lasts **6 hours**. Services of an English- or Spanish-speaking guide, transfers and lunch are listed as included. National park fees and the transit card are separate, excluded expenses. Check current fee amounts when booking, as government requirements may change.

## What you might see at Bachas

Lagoons behind the shore sometimes attract flamingos and other birds. Sea turtle nesting sites have been recorded around the beaches. That does not mean turtles or flamingos will be visible on every day or in every season.

Binoculars make birdwatching easier, while wildlife photography should be done without flash. The sea shore and lagoon offer different scenes, so allow time for both if visiting them is permitted and included by your guide.

The name Bachas is associated with remains of World War II-era barges discovered in this part of Santa Cruz. Their history is a small but interesting detail of a coastal walk.

## How Bachas differs from North Seymour

| Place | Main interest |
|---|---|
| [Bachas](/ecuador/place/bachas-beaches/) | Beaches and lagoons |
| [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) | Bird colonies |

On Seymour, visitors follow permitted paths among dry vegetation and observe seabirds. At Bachas, sand, sea and lagoons dominate the landscape. If swimming or snorkeling is scheduled, whether these activities are possible depends on actual conditions and the authorized format of the day.

Do not book this excursion expecting a guaranteed full day of beach relaxation: it also involves a boat crossing and a nature walk on another island.

## National park rules and preparation

In Galápagos National Park, visitors must follow their authorized guide's instructions, remain on permitted trails and keep their distance from animals. Conservation organizations recommend staying at least 2 meters away from wildlife, even when an animal approaches on its own. Feeding or touching animals is prohibited.

For the marine excursion, bring sun protection, water, suitable shoes for landing, a windproof layer on the boat and protection for electronics against spray. Swimming, the order of stops and crossing conditions depend on the weather, permits and specific boat route.

To compare other nature activities, explore [nature and wildlife journeys](/interests/wildlife/) and separate excursions to Ecuador's islands. The decision to visit Bachas is often closely tied to an interest in neighboring North Seymour.

## Frequently asked questions about Bachas excursions

### Can Bachas be visited together with North Seymour?

Yes. Our catalog features a combined [North Seymour and Bachas excursion](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/north-seymour-island-tour/).

### Are flamingos guaranteed?

No. They visit the lagoons, but their presence depends on natural conditions.

### Are all national park fees included?

The standalone program lists park fees and the transit card as separate expenses. Check their current amounts and payment procedures before departure.

### Is swimming permitted at Bachas?

The coast is known as a beach stop, but swimming on a particular day depends on weather, park rules and your guide's plan.

### In which language is the excursion conducted?

Ada Tours' published program lists English- and Spanish-speaking guiding services.

## Excursions via Baltra: the Galápagos airport and trips to nearby islands

[Baltra](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/) is one of the main arrival points in the Galápagos Islands. It has an airport from which travelers continue to [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) or a cruise vessel. Thus a search for "Baltra excursions" usually concerns choosing an itinerary after landing rather than a separate sightseeing day on the island itself.

Our Baltra-linked itineraries offer two different nature experiences: a land excursion to the giant tortoises of Santa Cruz and a marine trip to Bartolomé. The important distinction is where most of the day takes place and what is actually included.

## Crossing the Itabaca Channel

Baltra and Santa Cruz are separated by the Itabaca Channel. After leaving the airport, travelers go to the crossing, cross by boat and continue across Santa Cruz to Puerto Ayora or their accommodation. Galápagos National Park describes this route in its official arrival guidance.

The contrast of natural environments is visible during the journey: Baltra's dry, rocky coast, turquoise channel waters and greener areas of Santa Cruz. Allow for the actual arrival time and island entry formalities when planning.

## Santa Cruz tortoises and lava tunnels excursion

[Santa Cruz Island: Giant Tortoises and Lava Tunnels](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/santa-cruz-island-tour/) is a separate **6-hour excursion**. After Baltra and the Itabaca Channel, the route passes through the island's highlands, where giant land tortoises can be observed in natural areas, followed by a visit to lava tunnels.

Our program includes an English- or Spanish-speaking guide, transfers and lunch. The national park entry fee and Galápagos transit card are listed separately. Do not treat them as included in the excursion price; confirm current amounts and payment procedures before flying.

This outing suits travelers who want to see terrestrial animals and volcanic geology without a boat journey to a distant island. Santa Cruz's highland landscape is markedly different from the dry northern part of Baltra.

## Marine excursion to Bartolomé Island

The [Bartolomé Island excursion](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/bartolome-island-boat-tour/) includes a boat crossing, a climb to the famous Pinnacle Rock viewpoint and time at the beach or for snorkeling. Baltra and Bartolomé are listed in the route, but the main natural attraction is the volcanic island, with lava slopes and coastal wildlife.

Snorkeling and a land excursion to tortoises are different activities. If underwater observation is your priority, check which swimming locations are permitted and exactly what the water-based part includes. We also offer a [standalone diving day with 2 dives](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/galapagos-two-dive-day/), requiring separate selection, preparation and compliance with safety regulations.

## Preparing for arrival

The Galápagos have special entry and biosecurity controls. The official park administration requires a transit card and baggage inspection to protect the islands from introduced organisms. Allow time on the first day for formalities, the channel crossing and transfers.

For a cruise, confirm the boarding point and arrangements for meeting your guide in advance. If you are staying on Santa Cruz, remember that the airport is on another island. Seeing "Galápagos" on both your ticket and hotel address does not mean the two are next door.

On longer itineraries, Baltra appears in the [Galápagos luxury yacht VIP cruise](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/) and the [Complete Ecuador for New Year journey](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/), for example. Compare these options by nights and actual landings on other islands. Find the overall selection in the [Ecuador tours catalog](/ecuador/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions

### Are Baltra and Santa Cruz the same island?

No. They are separated by the Itabaca Channel, which is crossed by boat.

### Can I see tortoises immediately after landing?

A six-hour Santa Cruz excursion offers this experience. Whether it fits your flight depends on arrival and transfer times.

### Is snorkeling included in every excursion via Baltra?

No. It is listed on the boat trip to Bartolomé, whereas the land excursion on Santa Cruz focuses on different attractions.

### Is an additional ticket required to visit the archipelago?

The Galápagos have separate entry fees and a transit card. Check payment arrangements against the national park's official guidance and your chosen itinerary.
